https://www.dw.com/en/iran-warns-countri.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JGT8 Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran's powerful Supreme National Security Council, has vowed Tehran will retaliate against further economic pressure from the US and its allies Image: tabnak Advertisement Iran on Saturday warned countries against joining the United States ' campaign to isolate the Iranian economy. "We declare to all countries... do not join the economic war waged by the United States," said Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, on state television. "Any country participating in the imposition of economic restrictions against us is considered an enemy," he added. As the war nears its six-month anniversary, US President Donald Trump announced earlier this week what he called the "most crushing economic operation" against Tehran . Should Trump "take action, our confrontation will be like an earthquake," said Rezaei. US urges others to back Iran sanctions Washington has also called on other governments to join its efforts to ramp up economic pressure against Iran. But China , one of Iran's top strategic partners, has criticized the new campaign, arguing that "sanctions and pressure will not help resolve the issue." "China calls on all relevant parties to take responsible measures and resolve the problem through political and diplomatic means," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told reporters on Friday. The United Arab Emirates , a major trading partner for sanctioned Iran, already announced on Wednesday that it was cutting all financial and economic ties with Tehran until further notice. The decision was made in "light of escalations that undermine peace and security in the region," the UAE said in a statement . US-Iran war: Will it ever end? US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to hold a press conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday to give further details of the economic measures against Iran. "This is going to be the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world. And we are going to them and saying you are either with us or against us,” Bessent said.
